Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: Pullman by night? In THIS old heap? That mountain eats such rides for cheap.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: "Any idea what the weather is doing up at the pass?"
Result/Response: Past North Bend it's chains or a prayer — I hear it's a whiteout up there.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: "Here's a dollar, pal. I hope you spend it fair."
Result/Response: A giver! How noble, chum — I need fifty, yet you've provided one.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: "This is not the establishment for me. Time to dip."
Result/Response: He salutes you with a cup he found on the ground — "Safe travels, moneybags. Try not to drown."

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: You made it this far, but it's about to get tricky. Buy some chains and make the road less slippy.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "Are you selling those tire chains?"
Effect: Prices SNOW CHAINS at $150 on the Les Schwasted menu (list $200), this stop only; reveals snow hazard; ends
Result/Response: "I don't carry stock in my truck — I run the counter at Schwasted's. Ask for me; it's $150 with your luck."

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "Can you do any better on the price of those chains? Say $80?"

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "How bad can it be up there, really?"
Result/Response: If you have to ask, friend, here's my advice — stay in North Bend tonight and sleep on it twice.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "I don't need chains. This isn't my first snowdeo."
Result/Response: "Snowdeo," he repeats, and spits in the slush. "They all say that on the way up the brush."

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: $120 — no receipt, no refund, no eye; that's my whole pitch, so buy or say bye.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "Deal. Write it up before I think it through."
Effect: Prices SNOW CHAINS at $120 on the Les Schwasted menu, this stop only; reveals snow hazard; ends
Result/Response: "$120, then. Tell the counter I sent you — and don't expect paperwork when you do."

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "Fine — full price, then. You win."
Result/Response: You can pay full price here, or up there. It's much cheaper here.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "I'll take my chances. Walk away."
Result/Response: "Suit yourself," he shrugs, already turned — "the tow bill's steeper, but some folks like to learn."

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Bad enough I'm here and not in bed — whiteout up top, and the plows are losing, it's said.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "Not bad… if you have chains."
Effect: Returns to node: greet; reveals snow hazard

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: "Appreciate the offer, but I think I got this."
Result/Response: "Everybody's got it," he says, "'til they don't. I'd wish you luck, but honestly — I won't."

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: Past the tunnel it's whiteout, thick and dread — slow is smooth, and smooth is not-dead.

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: "Let me grab one of those thermoses off you."
Result/Response: This coffee is so strong it could strip a door — you'll be wide awake and craving more.

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: "Is there a safer route to take? I don't want to end up in the lake."
Result/Response: It's crazy up there. Kind of storm only the bold would dare.

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: "Thanks, but no thanks."
Result/Response: No worries, my guy. Stay alert, keep the road in your eyes.

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: My company card was just declined. Can you help me fill half the tank? My timeline is already behind.

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: "I can't afford that kind of cash. Any idea what the road ahead holds? I'm hoping not to crash."
Result/Response: It's going to be a wild ride. If the wind takes you, you wouldn't be the first who died.

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: "It's your lucky day. My pockets are blessed and I'm willing to pay."
Result/Response: He siphons you a fat share off his own tank — "Company's problem now," he says, and you've got him to thank. (70%) / Half the diesel he swore he'd hand — that's trucker math, you understand. (30%)

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: "Good luck with all that!"
Result/Response: "Yeah," he says, to the wind and no one — "luck. That's the one thing out here they don't run."

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: You can fill up at any fuel stop. But I've got a mix that makes your mileage pop.

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: "I'll take you up on that rocket fuel."
Result/Response: Dang! The tank reads impossibly full — whatever that was, it's got some pull. (80%) / That was NOT just gas, it's plain — the engine coughs and bucks in pain. (20%)

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: "Anything I should expect to see on the road ahead?"
Result/Response: Watch for tractors slow as tree pitch — they own the road, and every ditch.

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: "You're very generous, but you make me nervous."
Result/Response: He caps the can and grins with half a tooth — "Smart man. Most folks can't handle the truth."

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: Our app dodges every speed trap in this state — the free tier is what the reviewers hate.

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: "I'll support your vision. Sign me up for the annual subscription."
Result/Response: It actually works — two traps glide by unseen; she's already pitching a Series B, it seems. (70%) / 'Servers are scaling!' she chirps — then the app falls flat; and so does your hundred, just like that. (30%)

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: "It's not the cops I dread, but more of the weather. Do you know what lies ahead…"
Result/Response: The precip is mostly in the mountain heights, leaving Issaquah foggy AF. Might be worth upgrading to some fog lights.

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: "You won't fool me. I know you collect info and track my location."
Result/Response: "We call it telemetry," she says, unbowed — "and you agreed to it, out loud, in a crowd."

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: I need a pass-bound lift, that's true — cash up front, I won't even talk to you.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: "Lucky for you, I need the cash and have room for one more ass."
Result/Response: She pays, reads the curves better than your GPS could, then's gone at the summit — a passenger good. (60%) / Turns out she's on some watch-list, it seems — now you're right beside it, in the cops' bad dreams. (40%)

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: "I don't really have the space. Do you know about the weather at the mountain's base?"
Result/Response: I heard it's dumping buckets of rain in North Bend. Hope your wipers are prepared for full send.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: "Mom said not to talk to strangers."
Result/Response: "Your mom sounds smart," she says, thumb still out — "shame she raised whatever this is about."

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: Elk cross at dusk and don't check their blind side — and neither, it seems, do you when you ride.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: "Great advice. I'll keep my eyes out and my foot down."
Result/Response: Slow at the tree lines, mind your speed — they're bigger than your car's whole creed.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: "I heard you're looking for a lost hiker. I saw them at Commonwealth up at the pass."
Result/Response: She radios it in, thrown off the scent — your record breathes; the heat's misspent.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: "Those elk better watch out for me!"
Result/Response: She writes nothing down, which is somehow worse — "Seven hundred pounds," she says. "You first."

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Rodeo's in town, so the crowds are thick. But tip me well and I'll serve you quick.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "Whatever's hot, and keep the coffee coming."
Result/Response: Best call you've made the whole trip long — low bar, sure, but it's not wrong.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "What's ahead of me?"

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "This place smells like an ashtray. I'll get food on the road."
Result/Response: "Suit yourself, sugar," she says, unimpressed — "the gas station sushi is what you like best."

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Well, look who survived the road's mean tricks — same booth's free, and you're getting pie; don't fight it, that's the fix.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "I'll take the usual."
Result/Response: "The usual," she repeats. "Who ARE you?" — then the plate lands hot, like she always knew.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "Any news up the road?"

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "Just passing through — take care!"
Result/Response: "Take care yourself. And slower, if you're able — I'd hate to read your name across this table."

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Have you been to Vantage before? That wind can blow with the best of whores.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "Then load me up first. I'm not fighting that hungry."
Result/Response: Smart — nobody fights the wind and wins when their stomach's thin.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: "Noted. Thanks for the warning."
Result/Response: All morning the truckers came in white and green. Two hands on that wheel, and mind what's unseen.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Few stop in Hatton, dear, it's true — I keep gas for the ones who do, and cookies… but the gas is safer for you.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "I'll take the gas, ma'am. What's the damage?"
Result/Response: Drive safe, or don't, my dear — either way, the news'll reach my ear.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "Safer? What exactly is in those cookies?"

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "Why Hatton? There's nothing out here but wheat."

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "You're sweet, ma'am, but I've seen this movie."
Result/Response: "Everyone has, dear," she says, and waves — "and yet the road out here is still full of graves."

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Butter and sugar and a recipe old — one the county begged me to leave untold; one won't hurt you… or so I'm told.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "One cookie. For the road. What could go wrong?"
Result/Response: Strangely restoring, warm to the bone — you feel watched, but not alone. (70%) / You blink, and twenty minutes have flown — that's one fine cookie you've been thrown. (30%)

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "On second thought — let's stick to the gas."

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "I'm allergic to whatever that is."
Result/Response: "To butter?" she asks, and holds your eye too long — "or to something you can't name, but know is wrong?"

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Five hundred lived here once — two hotels, a bank, three elevators, electric light. Somebody's got to stay and mind what's left of the night.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "Where'd everybody go?"
Result/Response: West, mostly. The rest the road took its due — I just tidy up after, and wait on the few.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "…About that gas."

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: "Thank you, ma'am. I'll be going now. Slowly."
Result/Response: She watches you the whole way to the door — grandmothers in Hatton have done this before.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: Three wrecks a week I haul from this bend — business is good, which should worry you, friend.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: "What's it cost to have you on call before I need you?"
Result/Response: Crash, and I'll judge you — but only a bit; call it a discount on your fit.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: "Can you bang this dent out before I head on?"
Result/Response: A mallet, a grunt, a whack, a tad — and your car looks marginally less sad.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: "Three a week? What's actually putting them in the ditch?"
Result/Response: "Straight road, no lights, and nothing to see — they nod off at seventy and wake up in a tree."

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: "I don't plan on wrecking. That's the whole plan."
Result/Response: She laughs once, hard, and turns to walk away — "I'll leave the CB on anyway."

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: Basin-bound? Top your coolant off right here — past Vantage the shade quits and the gauge climbs, I fear.

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: "Top it off. I'd rather not boil over out there."
Effect: Prices COOLANT TOP-OFF at $25 on the Finesse menu (list $40), this stop only
Result/Response: "I don't keep jugs on me — I moonlight at Finesse. Ask inside, twenty-five, and say I said yes."

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: "Mind if I fill my jug off your hose?"
Result/Response: Warm hose water — not cold, but wet; he waves off your coins, says you owe him no debt.

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: "What am I actually watching for — the gauge, or something else?"
Result/Response: "Smell comes first — sweet, like syrup on the breeze. By the time that needle climbs, you're already on your knees."

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: "She's run this far. She'll run the rest."
Result/Response: They all run fine 'til the needle goes red. Then they run hot. Then they run dead.

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: Ice-cold lemonade, mister — best in the Basin, we swear! (It's also the ONLY one anywhere.)

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: "I'll take the whole pitcher. Keep the change."
Result/Response: Worth every cent that you're forgiving — your parched tongue rejoins the living.

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: "Just the one cup. I'm rationing."
Result/Response: Cold and impossibly sweet, that sip — you smack your lips and resume the trip.

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: "Straight answer: is there anything at all between here and the next town?"
Result/Response: "Circles of corn and a whole lot of sun." The taller one shrugs. "Dad says buy two. We only sell one."

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: "Shouldn't you two be in school?"
Result/Response: "It's August." They stare you flat down, unimpressed — you pull away feeling less than blessed.

Speaker: Swimsuit Girl
Text: Thorp goes dead quiet once the interstate clears — but the pool's still warm, and so are the beers.

Speaker: Swimsuit Girl
Text: "How much for a room? I'm running on fumes."
Result/Response: She flips you the key with a wink, sly and slow — "Shower's hot, bed's made… take it slow."

Speaker: Swimsuit Girl
Text: "I won't say no to a drink by the water."
Result/Response: Ice clinks in the glass she hands over, sincere — "On the house, cowboy. Long roads breed thirst, I hear."

Speaker: Swimsuit Girl
Text: "Is that old mill the only thing open around here?"
Result/Response: That mill shut down in '46, my dear. You're two hundred miles from anything here.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: I missed the last bus and my finals won't wait — I can pay; just drive like my mom's at the gate.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: Seatbelt. Both hands. Great. Perfect. Love it. Love this.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: You're doing great. I'm saying that for both of us.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: WE LIVED! Here — take it before I count it and change my mind.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Need a lift up the road a spell — I chip in for gas, don't scream, ride well, and tip good coin for a story you tell.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Music's yours. Pedal's yours. Impress me.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Is that all this thing does? ...Kidding. Mostly.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Decent run. Here's the fare, and here's a tip: nobody's ever impressed on the brakes.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: I need to be gone from here, and swift — and skip any cops, if you catch my drift.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: If anyone asks, I've been asleep since Tuesday.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: He checks the mirror more than you do. He has not blinked in a while.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: You never saw me. The money saw you, though. The money remembers.

Speaker: Ski Bum (passenger)
Location/Stop: Any stop (random offer) — NOTE: same name as the Snoqualmie Pass encounter NPC, different character

Speaker: Ski Bum (passenger)

Speaker: Ski Bum (passenger)

Speaker: Old-Timer
Text: Truck died. There's a doctor waiting down the way, and my gut's older than your car — go easy, I pray.

Speaker: Old-Timer
Text: Drove this road before anybody bothered painting lines on it.

Speaker: Old-Timer
Text: Mind the bumps, son. Breakfast is negotiating.

Speaker: Old-Timer
Text: Smoother than my nephew, and he does this for a living. Don't tell him.

Speaker: Crowd chatter

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Twede's is running Twin Peaks again. Order the pie. Do NOT order the coffee.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Chains next door are marked up four hundred percent and every single person is buying them.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Pass closes in three hours. MOVE.

Speaker: Crowd chatter

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Bakery's got the salted caramel ones. Ten minutes, tops. Ten.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Town had a live switchboard operator until 1966. Still can't get anyone to pick up.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Rivalry game tonight — half of Pullman is already on this road ahead of you.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Coffee's on. You look like hell. Both of those are facts.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Troopers sit around Kittitas this time of night. They love a quota.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Somebody's climbing up to the steel horses. In flip-flops. At night.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Last gas before the basin. I'm not being dramatic. Last gas.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Wind's up. If you've got anything on the roof, it's already gone.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Free apples in the orchard. Free-ish. Don't get caught.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: My uncle swears every cop in this town plays poker on Fridays. It's Friday.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Desert sunset in twenty minutes and you're going to miss it. Floor it.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Truck stop taqueria. Life-changing. I'm not exaggerating and I'm not eating anywhere else.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: You skipped Royal? They had the good energy drinks. The ones that are basically illegal.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Combines on 26 tonight. Those things are rolling roadblocks with lights.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Population two hundred. One cop. Do not test him.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Somebody's grandma sent cookies for the party. Nobody can figure out whose grandma.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Last shower for fifty miles. Consider that carefully.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: You're basically there. Do not blow it now.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Everyone is asking where the f— you are. Everyone.

Speaker: Crowd chatter
Text: Pullman's lit up like a Christmas tree. You can see it from the hill.

Speaker: Huff's Attendant
Text: Pump six is honest, pump four is a liar — pay inside or you'll stand here 'til you retire.

Speaker: CarGo Dispatcher
Text: Freight's freight and the clock doesn't care — load's out back if you're headed there.

Speaker: CowBella Shopkeeper
Text: Everything in here is orange, lethal, or both — pick one and I'll spare you the safety oath.

Speaker: AOK Camp Host
Text: Tents, tarps, and a stove that half-works — everything you need to regret the outdoors and its perks.

Speaker: Lord Motors Manager
Text: Every car on this lot runs. That's the pitch. Past that, we negotiate which.

Speaker: Sam's Owner
Text: Sam's not here. Sam is never here. I do the wrenching and Sam does the beer.

Speaker: Gas-N-Sip Clerk
Text: Coolers on the left, regrets on the right — I quit judging people around midnight.

Speaker: AM/BM Clerk
Text: Whatever you're after, don't say it out loud. Point, pay, and go rejoin the crowd.

Speaker: Metro Park & Ride Courier
Text: I move what fits in a trunk and don't ask — point me at yours and name the task.

Speaker: Les Schwasted Tech
Text: Free beef with every set of tires. Long story. Don't ask about the fires.

Speaker: Finesse Technician
Text: You want it fast, or you want it pretty? Both costs double. That's the city.
